title: Work site insecticide, herbicide and fungicide application preparation processes

lessons.title: Preparing sites for application at work
lessons.html:
Your role in this module

In the workplace you will prepare many sites for spray, bait and dust applications: kitchens and homes, offices, food stores, farm sheds, silo perimeters, fence lines and orchards. Under your mentor's supervision you will practise the full preparation routine until you can do it reliably on your own.

A preparation routine to practise

  1. Confirm the job card: site, areas, target pest, product, rate and method.
  2. Send or confirm client preparation instructions.
  3. On arrival, walk the area with the client and check that preparation has been done.
  4. Clear people and animals and agree re-entry times.
  5. Protect food, utensils, water troughs, feed, fish tanks and electronics.
  6. Place warning notices and barriers.
  7. For outdoor work, check wind, rain and buffer zones around water, crops and hives.
  8. Set up the mixing area on an impermeable surface away from water, with a spill kit.
  9. Check and test equipment with clean water.
  10. Read the label again, then mix the calculated quantity wearing PPE.
  11. Hold a short toolbox talk before application starts.

Scenario: farm workers' housing

You are preparing to treat cockroaches in farm workers' houses. Some families have not emptied their cupboards and one has a baby. With your mentor you explain the preparation again respectfully, help where appropriate, and agree that the house with the baby will be treated with gel bait only, placed out of reach. You reschedule one house where food could not be removed. This shows that preparation is about people as much as products.

lessons.title: Quality, safety and evidence
lessons.html:
Common preparation mistakes

MistakeConsequence
Starting without checking client preparationFood or toys contaminated
Mixing next to a borehole or tapWater contamination
Not checking wind before herbicide workDrift damage to crops or gardens
Not testing equipment with waterLeaks onto the operator, wrong output
No noticesPeople enter wet treated areas
Skipping the labelWrong rate, PPE or re-entry time

Safety behaviour you must show

  • Wearing the PPE specified on the label every time.
  • Never eating, drinking or smoking during preparation and mixing.
  • Keeping concentrates in original labelled containers and never decanting into food or drink containers.
  • Never leaving products or mixed spray unattended.
  • Knowing where the first aid kit, emergency water, label and SDS are.

Evidence for your portfolio

  • Completed pre-start checklists signed by you and your mentor.
  • Calculation records for mixes.
  • Calibration records.
  • Client preparation instruction sheets.
  • Reflections, for example on a job you postponed and why.

Key points

  • Follow the full preparation routine on every job, from job card to toolbox talk.
  • Check client preparation and adapt for vulnerable people, or reschedule.
  • Mix on an impermeable surface away from water, with PPE and a spill kit.
  • Check weather and buffer zones before outdoor work.
  • Keep checklists, calculations and calibration records as evidence.
